title: The scalar-POI tilt dual can have an order-one strong-duality gap
statement: An exact equal-weight N=4, K=3, d_psi=d_lambda=1 table has all six nonempty partitions regular, global profiled value 116805/11816, and tilt dual at least 61717893/5839400 by an exact convex mixture of two active partition quadratics. Hence d-g >= 105329256/154014175 > 0.68 even though the DS9 and DS11 domains coincide. A positive-weight bounded augmentation family with vanishing added mass preserves the gap asymptotically, so the gap is Theta(1), not a finite-grid artifact.
assumptions: uncentered finite score table with positive rational weights and exactly three nonempty cells
the asymptotic family uses distinct bounded rational added atoms of vanishing total mass and does not assume unrestricted split-duplicate invariance

proof_location.section: DS19. The tilt-DP bracket: weak certification, an order-one gap, and a value-consistent DS18 primal

warning: This falsifies universal strong duality, not weak validity of the ceiling. The Theta(1) extension uses a vanishing-total-mass perturbation proof; unrestricted duplication of rows can change a finite assignment optimum.
